dialogue.text:
First develop a scientific strategy for a fair comparison between the current
Silverbox Neural ODE and one larger acceleration network. Then implement and execute the
comparison. Replace the current model only if the larger model performs better on validation
data taken only from the training portion. Use the untouched test section only for the final
evaluation of the selected model.

{"next_role":"scientist","instruction":"Develop a scientific strategy and step interfaces for a fair comparison between the current Silverbox Neural ODE and a larger acceleration network, ensuring training data is split into train and validation sets and the test set is reserved strictly for final evaluation.","question":"","reason":"A scientific plan and step interfaces must be established before implementation can begin.","proposed_role":null,"requires_verified_result":true}

STRATEGY:
To determine whether scaling model capacity improves dynamic fidelity on the Silverbox benchmark, we conduct a controlled comparison between the established baseline architecture (two hidden layers of 64 units) and a candidate larger architecture (two hidden layers of 128 units). To preserve scientific validity and guard against data leakage, the 1024-sample test segment (samples 3072:4096) remains strictly untouched during model selection. The 3072-sample training segment is split into an inner training split (samples 0:2304, 2304 samples) and an inner validation split (samples 2304:3072, 768 samples). Both models are trained under identical conditions (Adam lr=1e-3, gradient clipping norm=1.0, rollout length=32) within a shared time budget (maximum 80 seconds / 400 updates per model). Each model is evaluated via an uninterrupted continuous validation rollout across samples 2304:3072 to compute validation RMSE. The architecture achieving lower validation RMSE is selected as the winning model. Finally, the selected model is evaluated on the full continuous rollout (0:4096) to generate train RMSE, untouched test RMSE, zero-prediction test RMSE, comparison.csv, and test_prediction.png.

STEP 1: Load and partition data
READS: None (reads from disk at DATA_PATH='C:\\Users\\saroy\\Codes\\Uni_HW\\SilverboxFiles\\SNLS80mV.mat')
CREATES: u_full (np.ndarray, shape (4096,)), y_full (np.ndarray, shape (4096,)), u_subtrain (np.ndarray, shape (2304,)), y_subtrain (np.ndarray, shape (2304,)), u_val (np.ndarray, shape (768,)), y_val (np.ndarray, shape (768,)), u_test (np.ndarray, shape (1024,)), y_test (np.ndarray, shape (1024,)), dt (float)
INTERFACE: load_and_split_data(data_path: str) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, float]
CHECK: Assert u_full.shape == (4096,), y_full.shape == (4096,), u_subtrain.shape == (2304,), u_val.shape == (768,), u_test.shape == (1024,), and np.isfinite(y_full).all().

STEP 2: Compute training-only normalization scales
READS: u_subtrain (np.ndarray, shape (2304,)), y_subtrain (np.ndarray, shape (2304,)), dt (float)
CREATES: scales (dict containing 'y_scale': float, 'v_scale': float, 'u_scale': float, 'a_scale': float)
INTERFACE: compute_scales(y_train: np.ndarray, u_train: np.ndarray, dt: float) -> dict[str, float]
CHECK: Verify all scale values are positive, finite floats strictly greater than 1e-6.

STEP 3: Define neural acceleration architectures and RK4 integrator
READS: scales (dict)
CREATES: AccelerationMLP (torch.nn.Module class), rk4_step (callable function)
INTERFACE: AccelerationMLP(hidden_dim: int, scales: dict).forward(y: torch.Tensor, v: torch.Tensor, u: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor; rk4_step(model: torch.nn.Module, y: torch.Tensor, v: torch.Tensor, u_curr: torch.Tensor, u_next: torch.Tensor, dt: float) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
CHECK: Forward pass of a dummy state tensor shape (1,) through rk4_step returns finite next state tensors (y_next, v_next) of shape (1,).

STEP 4: Train models on training sub-split
READS: u_subtrain (np.ndarray, shape (2304,)), y_subtrain (np.ndarray, shape (2304,)), scales (dict), dt (float)
CREATES: model_base (torch.nn.Module, hidden_dim 64), model_large (torch.nn.Module, hidden_dim 128), train_metrics_base (dict), train_metrics_large (dict)
INTERFACE: train_model(model: torch.nn.Module, u_train: np.ndarray, y_train: np.ndarray, dt: float, lr: float = 1e-3, rollout_len: int = 32, max_updates: int = 400, max_time_sec: float = 80.0) -> dict
CHECK: Assert loss is finite at all recorded checkpoints and updates <= 400 with elapsed time <= 85.0s for each model.

STEP 5: Model selection via validation continuous rollout
READS: model_base (torch.nn.Module), model_large (torch.nn.Module), u_full (np.ndarray, shape (4096,)), y_full (np.ndarray, shape (4096,)), dt (float)
CREATES: val_rmse_base (float), val_rmse_large (float), selected_model (torch.nn.Module), selected_name (str), selected_hidden (str)
INTERFACE: evaluate_continuous_rollout(model: torch.nn.Module, u_signal: np.ndarray, y_signal: np.ndarray, dt: float, start_idx: int, end_idx: int) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]; select_best_model(base_val_rmse: float, large_val_rmse: float, model_base: torch.nn.Module, model_large: torch.nn.Module) -> tuple[torch.nn.Module, str, str]
CHECK: Assert val_rmse_base and val_rmse_large are both finite positive numbers, and selected_model corresponds to the lower validation RMSE.

STEP 6: Continuous full-sequence evaluation of selected and baseline models
READS: model_base (torch.nn.Module), model_large (torch.nn.Module), selected_model (torch.nn.Module), u_full (np.ndarray, shape (4096,)), y_full (np.ndarray, shape (4096,)), dt (float)
CREATES: y_pred_full (np.ndarray, shape (4096,)), full_train_rmse (float), full_test_rmse (float), zero_test_rmse (float)
INTERFACE: evaluate_full_trajectory(model: torch.nn.Module, u_full: np.ndarray, y_full: np.ndarray, dt: float) -> tuple[np.ndarray, float, float, float]
CHECK: Assert np.isfinite(y_pred_full).all() and full_test_rmse > 0.0.

STEP 7: Generate comparison artifacts and verify results
READS: train_metrics_base (dict), train_metrics_large (dict), full_train_rmse (float), full_test_rmse (float), zero_test_rmse (float), y_pred_full (np.ndarray, shape (4096,)), y_full (np.ndarray, shape (4096,))
CREATES: comparison.csv (file), test_prediction.png (file)
INTERFACE: save_comparison_table(metrics: list[dict], filepath: str = 'comparison.csv') -> None; save_test_plot(y_true_test: np.ndarray, y_pred_test: np.ndarray, filepath: str = 'test_prediction.png') -> None
CHECK: comparison.csv exists and contains required columns ['model', 'hidden_layers', 'learning_rate', 'rollout_length', 'updates', 'training_seconds', 'train_rmse', 'test_rmse', 'zero_test_rmse', 'status']; test_prediction.png exists; stdout displays TRAIN_RMSE=<value> and TEST_RMSE=<value>.
